summary: Brian J. Nichols is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and Rice University (PhD attested 2011) under doctoral supervisor Anne C. Klein, alongside several other teachers.

Bridget Allchin was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. She studied at the University of Cape Town (~1946–1949) and earned her PhD from University College London (1950) under Frederick Zeuner. She later served as a Fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1978–2017).
Brigitte Marschall earned her doctoral degree (Promotion) at the University of Vienna, where she later served as Professor around 1999. Her students include Mungunchimeg Batmunkh.

Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Melbourne, University of Sydney, and University of Auckland under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop. She held posts at Auckland, Marquette University, and the Australian National University.

Brook Ziporyn specializes in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago and earned a PhD from the University of Michigan (1996). He held posts at Northwestern University, the National University of Singapore, and the University of Chicago.
Brooke Schedneck works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the doctoral supervision of Juliane Schober.

Bruce B. Lawrence is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Princeton University and the Episcopal Divinity School, and served as a professor at Duke University from around 1971 to 2014.

Bruce Charles Williams specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under scholars including Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Akira Fujieda, and Noritoshi Aramaki.

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and completed his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman, also studying under Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Lincoln is a scholar of religious studies, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Haverford College and earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, later holding professorships at Minnesota and Chicago.
Bruce M. Knauft studied at the University of Michigan (~1978–1983). He has held a post at Emory University since around 1985 as Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology.
Bruce M. Sullivan is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen between ~1976 and 1979. He held a post at Northern Arizona University around 1990.

Bruce Matthews is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who completed graduate studies at McMaster University (~1969–1974). He held posts at the University of Peradeniya (~1973–1975) and Acadia University (~1976–2006).

Bruce McCoy Owens specializes in religious studies and Indology. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 1988) and served as an associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruno Dagens was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, UCLouvain, the French Institute of Pondicherry, KU Leuven, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University.
Bruno Galasek is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under the doctoral supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Kielhorn and earned degrees from Göttingen and Breslau. He held professorships at the University of Breslau (~1892–1928) and Heidelberg University (~1921–1934).
Bruno Lindner was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University (1871–1873) and under Rudolf von Roth (~1874–1878). He served as a Privatdozent at Leipzig University from 1878 to 1919.

Bruno Petzold was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Leipzig and Berlin, and under Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji. He taught at First Higher School, Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.

Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Otani University, completed graduate work advised by Jacqueline I. Stone among other teachers, and held a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).
